title: Bug: 422 error when using Annotated[list[str], MinLen(1)] with repeated query params in Query() Pydantic model
body:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import MinLen

app = FastAPI()

class QueryModel(BaseModel):
    descriptions: Annotated[list[str], MinLen(1)] | None = None

@app.get("/test")
def test(query: QueryModel = Query()):
    return {"descriptions": query.descriptions}
```


### Description

Using a Pydantic model with `Annotated[list[str], MinLen(1)]` as a query parameter via `Depends()` causes a 422 error — even when multiple query parameters are passed (`?descriptions=a&descriptions=b`). This looks like a regression in the FastAPI + Pydantic v2 integration.

```
GET /test?descriptions=a&descriptions=b
```

should result in 

```
{
  "descriptions": ["a", "b"]
}
```

but results in

```
422 Unprocessable Entity
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "type": "list_type",
      "loc": ["query", "descriptions"],
      "msg": "Input should be a valid list",
      "input": "a"
    }
  ]
}
```

I know that this behavior works correctly if we use `Query(..., min_length=1)` directly in the route function or in model class but I think syntax with `Annotated` should be valid as well for collections if it can be used in all other cases

### Operating System

macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.12

### Pydantic Version

2.11.5

### Python Version

3.11.1

### Additional Context

_No response_
